Members of Tindig Hagonoy march through the streets of Hagonoy, Bulacan, on Sunday to mark the group’s first anniversary and renew their call for accountability over alleged corruption in flood control projects and solutions to the town’s chronic flooding problem.

HAGONOY, Bulacan — More than 300 residents marched through the streets of this municipality early Sunday to mark the first anniversary of Tindig Hagonoy, renewing their call for justice over alleged corruption in flood control projects and for concrete solutions to the town’s chronic flooding problem.

The protesters also called for accountability over the alleged billion-peso “ghost” flood control projects they blamed for worsening flooding that has repeatedly submerged much of the town, leaving residents helpless.

A year after Tindig Hagonoy first staged organized a march through flooded streets to protest alleged corruption in flood control projects, Saguinsin said residents are now waiting for the national government to deliver solutions, following assurances from Public Works and Highways Secretary Vince Dizon.

Tindig Hagonoy leader Renato dela Cruz told protesters after Sunday’s march that continued dialogues, meetings and assurances from Dizon have given the group hope that the flooding problem can finally be addressed.
Tindig Kalumpitenyo organized the People’s Rally for the second consecutive year, with more than 300 residents and various groups joining the demonstration.
They vowed that their protest would not end with Sunday’s rally and would continue until their calls for accountability and a lasting solution to the flooding are addressed.

Dressed in black, participants from various sectors—including teachers, workers, transport groups, fishermen, vendors, senior citizens, and youth—waded through flooded streets to demand accountability from officials.
The demonstration was organized by Tindig Hagonoy, which criticized the slow pace of investigations into flood control anomalies, noting that no individuals have been held liable.

Rodel Ponce, parish priest of Saint Anne’s National Shrine in Hagonoy — on Saturday hold an anti-corruption rally at the town’s public plaza, one of the few places in the municipality that remain dry during high tide.
The protests started with a Mass at 6 a.m.
at the National Shrine of Saint Anne’s, the parish church of Hagonoy, followed by the more than an hour of “lusong,” or a walk along the flooded streets of the villages of Sta.
Monica, San Sebastian, and Sto.

citations.quote: Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News CALUMPIT, Bulacan — Even after the rains brought by the southwest monsoon stopped, communities in Calumpit, Bulacan, remained submerged in floodwaters.
With the flooding persisting for nearly two months, residents took to the streets on Sunday to call for accountability and a permanent solution to the recurring floods.

CAN’T STAY DRY Despite improving weather, residents of Hagonoy town in Bulacan on Thursday wade through flooded streets as water, accumulated from heavy rains dumped by recent storms and the prolonged “habagat” (southwest monsoon), has yet to recede.

MALOLOS CITY, Bulacan, Philippines — Even as incessant rains have eased, 116 barangays in Bulacan remain submerged in one foot to six feet of floods, with 8,728 people still sheltered in evacuation sites, the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office said yesterday.
He noted that Hagonoy and Paombong were flooded because of the high tide and the floods receding in nearby Pampanga and Nueva Ecija provinces.

Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News MANILA - Several areas in Quezon City and Bulacan were flooded following hours of Habagat-induced heavy rains, prompting local authorities to carry out preemptive and forced evacuations in flood-prone communities.
Flooding also continued in parts of Calumpit, Hagonoy, and Malolos.
The said villages in Calumpit and in Hagonoy are still under 1-2 feet of flood water even though it is no longer raining the past few days.

“Ang dami pa rin po nating mga barangay na lagpas tao at lubog. Marami pa rin po mga sektor at mga mamamayang Kalumpitenyo hanggang sa ngayon na hindi pa rin nakapagahanap buhay ng matino,” Tindig Kalumpitenyo spokesperson Zul Kifli Magat said.

Bulacan declares state of calamity amid widespread flooding Residents voiced their frustration over the recurring floods, saying the problem has affected not only their homes but also their livelihoods and their children’s education.

Dressed in black, participants from various sectors—including teachers, workers, transport groups, fishermen, vendors, senior citizens, and youth—waded through flooded streets to demand accountability from officials.
Tindig Hagonoy waded into the flood as they showed their frustration at the continued flooding of their hometown where they think local and national governments could do nothing.

During the “Managot Ang Dapat Managot” interfaith prayer vigil on Sunday, Faustino said Domingo has to explain to the people what happened to the projects as residents continue to suffer from flooding.
Tindig Hagonoy conducted an indignation rally on Saturday, marching and wading through the town’s flooded streets to denounce corruption in infrastructure projects.

Members of Tindig Hagonoy march through the streets of Hagonoy, Bulacan, on Sunday to mark the group’s first anniversary and renew their call for accountability over alleged corruption in flood control projects and solutions to the town’s chronic flooding problem.

The protesters also called for accountability over the alleged billion-peso “ghost” flood control projects they blamed for worsening flooding that has repeatedly submerged much of the town, leaving residents helpless.

A year after Tindig Hagonoy first staged organized a march through flooded streets to protest alleged corruption in flood control projects, Saguinsin said residents are now waiting for the national government to deliver solutions, following assurances from Public Works and Highways Secretary Vince Dizon.
CITY OF MALOLOS—The Bulacan provincial board on Thursday placed the province under a state of calamity due to massive floods following weeks of relentless rains brought by the monsoon season.

The local governments of the coastal towns of Calumpit, Hagonoy and Bulakan, which were swamped by as high as 1.82 meters (6 feet) of floodwaters, earlier declared a state of calamity in their respective municipalities.
PDRRMO chief Manuel Lukban Jr. said Barangay Meysulao in Calumpit town has the worst floods, with waters up to six feet as of yesterday morning.
The town has at least 28 barangays under floodwaters.
Lukban said 41 barangays in Malolos are flooded, followed by Hagonoy with 25, Paombong with 14, Bocaue and Guiguinto with seven each as well as Pulilan and Balagtas towns with four each.

“So ngayon naapektuhan tayo noh maliban doon sa regular natin na low lying areas ‘tong Calumpit, Hagonoy, Bulacan Bulacan, Malolos ay naapektuhan din naman ng higit na galing yung tubig galing sa mountain ranges natin, etong Marilao River.”
In Calumpit alone, around 5,600 individuals were evacuated, while more than 300 residents in Marilao were initially moved to safer areas as operations continued.

“Yung sa ano natin sa Calumpit ang low lying areas natin kasi kaninang umaga iyon, na conduct natin yung pre-emptive kahapon pa dun, so nasa 5,600 yun individuals. Ang ano ngayon ay nasa 5,600 individuals yun, yung ngayon dito sa Marilao on going pa ang operation ng pag pre-emptive nasa about 300 plus wala pang official number pero initial report nasa more than 300 na eh.,” Lukban said.

The governor expressed belief the only thing that can resolve the present flooding problem in the towns of Hagonoy and Calumpit is proper water management, particularly in the operation of the big turbine of Angat dam.
Calumpit and Hagonoy are low-lying towns and major catch basins in Bulacan.
He said the flood waters in Calumpit, particularly in the villages of San Jose;
and Santa Lucia remain due to the flood waters coming from the neighboring provinces of Pampanga and Nueva Ecija, and the continuous release of water from Bustos dam.
